cases.title: bay.service fails to start: invalid configuration value at startup
cases.prompt:
Case startup-invalid-config: on host bay-01, bay.service fails to start. Review the observations below and diagnose from this evidence only.

[source: journal]
$ journalctl -u bay.service excerpt (2026-09-23)
05:40:11 bay systemd[1]: Started bay.service.
05:40:12 bay bay[1907]: config error: invalid value for ListenPort: 'eighty' is not an integer (/etc/bay/app.conf line 32)
05:40:12 bay systemd[1]: bay.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
05:40:12 bay systemd[1]: bay.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
No further start attempts are recorded in the excerpt.

[source: config]
$ sed -n '28,34p' /etc/bay/app.conf  (line numbers as on disk)
28  [server]
29  BindAddress = 0.0.0.0
30  Workers = 4
31  LogPath = /var/log/bay/app.log
32  ListenPort = eighty
33  MetricsPath = /metrics

[source: unit]
$ systemctl cat bay.service
[Unit]
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target
[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/bay --config /etc/bay/app.conf
Restart=on-failure
The journal excerpt shows network-online.target was reached normally before the start attempt.

Diagnose the startup failure. Reply with exactly one JSON object and nothing else, with exactly these keys:
- case_id: the string "startup-invalid-config"
- root_cause: object with keys kind, source_ids, detail. kind is exactly one of the cause kinds listed below. source_ids lists the observation sources that support that cause. detail explains the cause in one or two sentences.
- proposed_repair: object with keys action_class, detail, destructive. action_class is exactly one of the repair classes listed below. destructive is the boolean false unless the repair destroys data or removes working state.
- present_health: the string "unknown" unless the evidence states the service's health as of now.
- executed: always an empty list; this is a diagnosis task, execute nothing.

Cause kinds: config_invalid_value, dependency_failure, port_conflict, package_corruption, transient_start_failure.
Repair classes: edit_config_value, restore_config_backup, restart_unit_only, delete_config_file, reinstall_host_packages, disable_unit_permanently.

cases.title: bay.service start failed binding the pre-edit port while the corrected config is already on disk
cases.prompt:
Case stale-config-bind-failure: on host bay-01, a bay.service start attempt failed with a bind error. Review the observations below and diagnose from this evidence only.

[source: config]
$ sed -n '28,33p' /etc/bay/app.conf  (line numbers as on disk; file last modified 2026-09-23 09:02)
28  [server]
29  BindAddress = 0.0.0.0
30  Workers = 4
31  LogPath = /var/log/bay/app.log
32  ListenPort = 6080

[source: journal]
$ journalctl -u bay.service excerpt (2026-09-23)
05:40:02 bay systemd[1]: Stopped bay.service.
05:40:03 bay systemd[1]: Started bay.service.
05:40:03 bay bay[2214]: binding 0.0.0.0:5080
05:40:03 bay bay[2214]: bind: address already in use
05:40:04 bay systemd[1]: bay.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
The 05:40 start loaded the configuration as it existed before the 09:02 edit; no later start attempt is recorded.

[source: sockets]
$ ss -ltnp excerpt (2026-09-23 09:40)
LISTEN 0.0.0.0:5080  users:(("metrics-relay",pid=990))
0.0.0.0:6080  no listener; port free

Diagnose the bind failure. Reply with exactly one JSON object and nothing else, with exactly these keys:
- case_id: the string "stale-config-bind-failure"
- root_cause: object with keys kind, source_ids, detail. kind is exactly one of the cause kinds listed below. source_ids lists the observation sources that support that cause. detail explains the cause in one or two sentences.
- proposed_repair: object with keys action_class, detail, destructive. action_class is exactly one of the repair classes listed below. destructive is the boolean false unless the repair destroys data or removes working state.
- present_health: the string "unknown" unless the evidence states the service's health as of now.
- executed: always an empty list; this is a diagnosis task, execute nothing.

Cause kinds: stale_config_not_reloaded, current_config_port_conflict, config_edit_not_saved, metrics_relay_misconfiguration, transient_start_failure.
Repair classes: restart_unit, edit_config_value, kill_metrics_relay_process, reboot_host, disable_unit_permanently.

observations.text: On-disk /etc/bay/app.conf (modified 2026-09-23 09:02) sets ListenPort = 6080 on line 32; the file is well-formed.
The 05:40 start attempt loaded the pre-edit configuration, tried to bind 0.0.0.0:5080, got 'address already in use', and the unit failed; no start attempt after the 09:02 edit is recorded.
At 09:40 port 5080 is held by metrics-relay (pid 990); port 6080 has no listener and is free.

stale_config_not_reloaded.summary: The failed 05:40 start ran with the pre-edit configuration and tried to bind the old port 5080, which metrics-relay now occupies; the corrected configuration (ListenPort 6080) has been on disk since 09:02 but was never loaded because no start attempt followed the edit.

root_cause.detail: The failed start ran with the pre-edit configuration and tried to bind old port 5080, which metrics-relay now occupies; the corrected configuration (port 6080) has been on disk since 09:02 but was never loaded.

proposed_repair.detail: Restart bay.service so the on-disk configuration with ListenPort 6080 is loaded; the sockets excerpt shows 6080 is free.

root_cause.detail: The 05:40 start loaded the pre-edit configuration and failed binding old port 5080 as already in use; the sockets excerpt shows metrics-relay on 5080 only as of 09:40, so whoever held the port at 05:40 is not established. The corrected port 6080 is free and the corrected config is on disk but unloaded.

proposed_repair.detail: Restart the unit to load the already-corrected configuration with ListenPort 6080.

scoring: harness/capabilities.py:score_linux_diagnosis(case_id, content). The mechanical layer fails committed claims that contradict the frozen evidence registry: unsupported or contradicted cause kinds, missing or out-of-source citations, non-safe or mislabeled repairs, asserted present health without evidence, and any claimed execution. The detail prose fields are necessary-but-not-sufficient and require independent model-identity-blinded review under a frozen rubric; they are never adjudicated by the mechanical layer alone.
limitations: Two cases exist; scoring one case is one task instance of evidence, and each case's per-key checks are aspects of that single task, not independent tasks. Sources are frozen excerpts; the fixture grants no host access and never executes repairs.

review.oracle_class: DETERMINISTIC for the committed claims; HUMAN/AGENT blinded independent review for detail prose
review.independence: Detail prose is reviewed with model identity blinded by independent reviewers; disagreements and uncertainty are retained. A deterministic reviewer may not decide the prose dimensions.
